newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks stagnant, Zagrebacka rises.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks stagnant, Zagrebacka rises.

text.p: Croatian stocks were stagnant at 1200 GMT on Thursday amid weak buying interest, except for rising blue chip Zagrebacka Banka, traders said.
The bank stock traded at 1,829 kuna, up from its 1,820 Wednesday close and 1,800 shares went in a single morning deal.
"Wait till these shares are sold in London, someone is making a pretty penny on the difference," said one trader with a large market share.
Zagrebacka's 1/10 GDRs fetched $31.12/31.25 on Seaq International.

Another fully-listed stock, Pliva pharmaceuticals, firmed one kuna to 421, but volume was said to be very small. Its GDRs, which represent 1/5 of each share, rose to $14.82 on the London Stock Exchange from $14.5 at the open.
Relatively cheap hoteliers attracted no buyers save for Riviera from Porec, selling some 200 units at 160 kuna each.
The lull in hotel stocks was thought to last till after Easter, reflecting tourist bookings for the summer. Foreign investors were expected to wait before venturing any money into seaside hoteliers.
Zagreb's Intercontinental Hotel, voted the best-run in the chain last year, was offered at 170 kuna, up five from its last deal earlier this month.
"I don't know why there is no interest, this is a good
stock," said Velimir Zelimorski of brokerage Fima.
